rule CobaltStrike_Beacon_Config {
    meta:
        description = "Detects embedded configuration in Cobalt Strike beacons"
        author = "SOC Team"
        reference = "https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0154/"
        tlp = "amber"
    strings:
        $a = { 2e 00 63 00 6f 00 6e 00 66 00 69 00 67 } // ".config" in wide Unicode
        $b = { 6d 65 6d 6f 72 79 20 61 6c 6c 6f 63 } // "memory alloc"
        $c = { 43 6f 62 61 6c 74 20 53 74 72 69 6b 65 } // "Cobalt Strike"
    condition:
        all of ($a, $b, $c)
}

arguments.summary: A credential compromise occurred on host WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42) belonging to user jsmith@corp.local in the Finance department. The initial access vector was a phishing email triggering malicious PowerShell execution from Outlook, leading to the deployment of Cobalt Strike Beacon via an encoded command. The payload was dropped as 'beacon.dll' in the user's Temp directory and executed via rundll32.exe. The malware established C2 communication over HTTPS to 198.51.100.23, performed host file modification, and attempted lateral movement via SMB. The beacon exhibits persistence via a registry run key and scheduled task, performs process injection, and includes keylogging capabilities. Detection occurred via IDS signature for Cobalt Strike beaconing, though initial execution was not blocked. No containment actions were executed due to lack of valid targets in Admin phase.
